about: Inputs from the platform's parity fixture (src/lib/engines/__tests__/fixtures/python-parity.json) plus one year-guard case; expected is the exact output of run(inputs). The platform's parity test checks these outputs against the Python reference engines of the 6 Nov 2026 A/B test (Malta: against an independent Python reference, mt-income-tax.test.ts).

headline.label: Take-home pay after income tax and employee NIC, 2026-27

steps: Adjusted net income = GBP 60,000.00 less gross relief-at-source contributions GBP 0.00 = GBP 60,000.00
Personal allowance = GBP 12,570.00
Taxable income = GBP 47,430.00; basic rate band GBP 37,700.00 at 20%, then 40% to GBP 125,140.00, then 45%
Income tax = GBP 11,432.00
Employee NIC = 8% of pay between GBP 12,570.00 and GBP 50,270.00 plus 2% above = GBP 3,210.60

constants_used.name: RATES

constants_used.name: TAPER_START
constants_used.quote: Allowance taper | £1 lost per £2 of adjusted net income above £100,000; nil at £125,140

constants_used.name: TAPER_ROUNDING
constants_used.value: round reduction up to whole pound
constants_used.section: The taxable base / Step 4: the Personal Allowance

constants_used.name: NIC_PRIMARY_THRESHOLD

constants_used.name: EE_NIC_UPPER_RATE
constants_used.quote: Employee Class 1 (category A) | 8% PT to UEL, 2% above
